During his tenure as Apple CEO, one of Tim Cook's most delicate tasks was walking a tightrope between defending the company's values and avoiding offending the White House, on issues ranging from immigration policy to diversity and inclusion.

After transitioning to the newly established role of executive chairman, he retains responsibility for government liaison, providing a degree of protection for his successor as CEO, John Ternus…

Past challenges

The challenges Cook has faced in the past go back several years. In 2018, for example, changes to US immigration policy and measures affected thousands of Apple employees. Cook joined other CEOs in writing to the government, pointing out that the changes caused "deep concern among many Apple employees" and carried "a risk of disrupting the company's operations".

Last year, Cook faced a similar dilemma when Trump demanded that Apple abandon its diversity and inclusion policies. In response, Cook said the company would comply with any legal changes, but would not abandon its own values.

Cook is now Apple's official diplomat

Apple has confirmed that Cook's new responsibilities include liaising with governments around the world.

Attending next week's White House dinner

Bloomberg reports that Cook will attend next week's White House state dinner for the Chinese president. US-China relations are currently at a tense moment, particularly on the issue of artificial intelligence.

9to5Mac take

I would venture to speculate that the idea of Cook taking on the diplomatic role was his own proposal. It is a selfless act designed to spare his successor unnecessary disruption and controversy.

Of course, Ternus will still face constraints when responding to controversial policies and legislation in the United States, China or elsewhere. But handing the responsibility for official responses to someone else does buy him more room to manoeuvre.
